title: Слово о пълку Игоревѣ
draftNote: Part IV — the poet's lament following the rout at the Kayala: nature mourns before any person speaks (grass drooping, a tree bent to the ground), the wrong done to Rus' (Обида) rises up and enters the land, brotherly strife breaks out afresh, the women of Rus' weep for husbands they will never see again, Kiev and Chernigov groan, the poet turns briefly to Svyatoslav's real 1184 victory over Kobyak, and closes with Igor's own defeat already sung of — and Igor blamed for it — as far off as Germany, Venice, Greece and Moravia, and Igor himself pictured dismounting from a golden saddle into a captive's.
source: Text: editio princeps — «Ироическая пѣснь о походѣ на половцовъ удѣльнаго князя Новагорода-Сѣверскаго Игоря Святославича», ed. A. I. Musin-Pushkin, Moscow, 1800 (public domain); via Russian Wikisource. 1800 orthography preserved. Prose sense-units at the edition's punctuation (no imposed verse lineation). Transliteration: scholarly Slavist romanization (ž š č c x; ě = ѣ; ŭ / ĭ = ъ / ь). Pronunciation: reconstructed late-12th-c. Old East Slavic (see slovo-audio doc); ж/ш/ц read hard by convention. Translations made fresh from the 1800 original.
about: This movement follows directly on the rout at the Kayala (part 3): the land itself mourns before any person speaks — grass drooping, a tree bending down in grief — and the poet names the wrong (Обида, 'offense, wrong') rising up among the Rus', personified as a maiden entering Troyan's land. Old strife between brothers breaks out afresh — 'this is mine, and that is mine too' — while the pagans overrun a divided Rus'; the women of Rus' weep for husbands they can no longer even picture in thought; Kiev and Chernigov groan under grief and misfortune. The poet then turns, briefly, from the disaster to Grand Prince Svyatoslav III's genuine, chronicled 1184 victory over the Polovtsian khan Kobyak — only to note that Igor's own defeat is already being sung of, and Igor himself blamed for it, as far off as the Germans, the Venetians (or Wends), the Greeks and the Moravians. The movement closes with Igor's capture pictured starkly: down from the golden saddle, into a captive's — and gladness itself drooping, in an echo (пониче) of the very word (ничить) that opened the movement's image of drooping grass. As throughout, several phrases here are genuine 'dark places' — жиръ and жирня времена, the gender mismatch in вступилъ, the identity of Карна и Жля — with no settled reading, flagged honestly rather than resolved with false confidence; the poem survives only in this 1800 edition, the medieval copy having burned in 1812.

sentences.t: Ничить трава жалощами, а древо стугою къ земли преклонилось.
sentences.tr: Ničitĭ trava žaloščami, a drevo stugoju kŭ zemli preklonilosĭ.
sentences.l: The grass droops with sorrows, and the tree has bent down to the earth with anguish.
sentences.i: The grass droops with grief, and the tree has bowed to the earth in anguish.
sentences.n: жалощами (instr. pl. of жалощи, 'sorrows,' cognate with modern жалость) and стугою (instr. sg., an old word for grief/anguish, closely related to туга 'grief,' used later in this same part) open this movement's mourning-nature personification: the grass and tree react to Rus's disaster before any person speaks. преклонилось is not an aorist but the l-participle perfect (neut. sg., agreeing with древо, 'tree') — Old East Slavic's ordinary past tense, distinct from the aorist forms (e.g. рече, ступаетъ→ступи) met elsewhere in the poem; most of this unit's and the next unit's verbs are this same perfect, not aorist.

sentences.t: Уже бо, братіе, не веселая година въстала, уже пустыни силу прикрыла.
sentences.tr: Uže bo, bratie, ne veselaja godina vŭstala, uže pustyni silu prikryla.
sentences.l: Already, brothers, an unjoyful season has arisen; already desolation has covered [our] strength.
sentences.i: Already, brothers, joy's season has passed; already desolation has swallowed up our strength.
sentences.n: въстала and прикрыла are again l-participle perfects, feminine singular, agreeing with година ('season, time') and пустыни respectively — not aorists. пустыни is nominative singular here (an old feminine i-stem noun, like кънягыни 'princess,' not a plural of пустыня 'desert') — 'desolation, wasteland' as the subject that 'has covered our strength.' This begins the poet's own direct lament, following the nature-image of unit 1.

sentences.t: Въстала обида въ силахъ Дажь-Божа внука.
sentences.tr: Vŭstala obida vŭ silaxŭ Daž-Boža vŭnuka.
sentences.l: Wrong has arisen among the forces of Dazhbog's grandson.
sentences.i: Wrong itself has risen up among the forces of Dazhbog's grandson.
sentences.n: обида ('offense, wrong, injury') is personified as an actor here and in the next unit, pictured entering the land like a maiden. Дажь-Божа внука ('Dazhbog's grandson') is the same collective epithet, met in part 3, for the people and princes of Rus' as descendants of the pagan sun-god Dazhbog; here it is grammatically singular, most likely standing for the Rus' collectively rather than one named prince. The 1800 edition spells the god's name Дажь-Божа here, without the д kept in part 3's Даждь-Божа — an orthographic inconsistency of the source itself, kept as printed rather than regularized.

sentences.t: Вступилъ дѣвою на землю Трояню, въсплескала лебедиными крылы на синѣмъ море у Дону плещучи, убуди жирня времена.
sentences.tr: Vstupilŭ děvoju na zemlju Trojanju, vŭspleskala lebedinymi kryly na siněmŭ more u Donu pleščuči, ubudi žirnja vremena.
sentences.l: [She] stepped as a maiden onto the land of Troyan, clapped with swan-wings upon the blue sea, splashing by the Don, [and] awoke [times of] plenty.
sentences.i: She stepped, a maiden, onto the land of Troyan, clapped swan-wings upon the blue sea by the Don, splashing — and stirred up years of plenty.
sentences.n: One of this part's densest dark places. Вступилъ is masculine in form (-лъ), yet the subject carried over from unit 3 is the feminine обида; most editors emend to вступила, but we keep the 1800 print's masculine form and flag the mismatch rather than emend it — it may be a misprint, or the grammatical subject may have silently shifted in a way no longer recoverable. жирня времена ('fat, abundant times') is likewise debated: it may mean the peaceful, prosperous years now disturbed, or carry an ironic sense lost to us; no reading commands consensus, and we do not claim more certainty than survives. Троянь recurs from parts 1 and 3, still unidentified.

sentences.t: Усобица Княземъ на поганыя погыбе, рекоста бо братъ брату: се мое, а то моеже; и начяша Князи про малое, се великое млъвити, а сами на себѣ крамолу ковати: а поганіи съ всѣхъ странъ прихождаху съ побѣдами на землю Рускую.
sentences.tr: Usobica Knjazemŭ na poganyja pogybe, rekosta bo bratŭ bratu: se moe, a to moeže; i načjaša Knjazi pro maloe, se velikoe mlŭviti, a sami na sebě kramolu kovati: a poganii sŭ vsěxŭ stranŭ prixoždaxu sŭ pobědami na zemlju Ruskuju.
sentences.l: The princes' strife against the pagans came to nothing, for brother said to brother: 'this is mine, and that also is mine'; and the princes began to speak of the small thing as the great, and to forge treachery among themselves; and the pagans came from every land, with victories, upon the land of Rus'.
sentences.i: What should have been the princes' war against the pagans came to nothing, for brother said to brother, 'This is mine, and that is mine too' — the princes took to inflating small matters into great ones and forging treachery among themselves, while the pagans poured in from every side, victorious, upon the land of Rus'.
sentences.n: усобица normally means internal feud among kinsmen (as in part 3); here it names, paradoxically, what should have been a shared campaign against the pagans, which 'perished' (погыбе, aorist 3sg) in princely quarreling — the poem's central charge, made concrete by the quoted quarrel. рекоста is a true dual aorist ('the two said' — a generic 'brother to brother,' not naming individuals). млъвити ('to noisily assert, wrangle over') governing 'се великое' ('this as great') pictures petty disputes inflated into major ones. поганіи, 'the pagans,' is the poem's standing name for the Polovtsians.

sentences.t: О! далече зайде соколъ, птиць бья къ морю: а Игорева храбраго плъку не крѣсити.
sentences.tr: O! daleče zajde sokolŭ, pticĭ bĭja kŭ morju: a Igoreva xrabrago plŭku ne krěsiti.
sentences.l: O! Far has the falcon flown, striking birds, [on its way] to the sea — but Igor's brave army is not to be raised up again.
sentences.i: O, far has the falcon flown, striking down birds on its way to the sea — but there is no reviving Igor's brave host.
sentences.n: The falcon-in-flight image, applied to Igor and his men throughout the poem, turns elegiac here: however far and fierce Igor's own flight, his army itself is now beyond recall. крѣсити ('to revive, raise up') shares its root with воскресение, 'resurrection,' in later Church Slavonic and Russian. The mid-part О! is a rare vocative outcry, the poet's own grief breaking through the narrative.

sentences.t: За нимъ кликну Карна и Жля, по скочи по Руской земли, смагу мычючи въ пламянѣ розѣ.
sentences.tr: Za nimŭ klyknu Karna i Žlja, po skoči po Ruskoj zemli, smagu myčjuči vŭ pljameně rozě.
sentences.l: After him Karna and Zhlya cried out, and sprang across the land of Rus', carrying scorching grief in a flaming horn.
sentences.i: Behind him rose the cries of Karna and Zhlya, racing across the land of Rus', bearing grief like flame in a burning horn.
sentences.n: Карна and Жля are personifications built directly from mourning-words — Карна from карити, 'to lament the dead' (cf. Slavic funeral-wailing vocabulary), Жля from жаль, 'pity, sorrow' — rather than named figures of an attested pagan pantheon; older, 19th-century scholarship sometimes called them goddesses of grief, but we present them here as personified cries, not confirmed cult figures. кликну and скочи are aorists, though their singular form does not strictly match the two-part subject Карна и Жля — a looseness of the poem's syntax we note rather than resolve. смагу ... въ пламянѣ розѣ ('scorching grief in a flaming horn') is another genuinely obscure image, kept literal rather than smoothed into an easier sense.

sentences.t: Жены Рускія въсплакашась аркучи: уже намъ своихъ милыхъ ладъ ни мыслію смыслити, ни думою сдумати, ни очима съглядати, а злата и сребра ни мало того потрепати.
sentences.tr: Ženy Ruskyja vŭsplakašasĭ arkuči: uže namŭ svoixŭ milyxŭ ladŭ ni mysliju smysliti, ni dumoju sdumati, ni očima sŭgljadati, a zlata i srebra ni malo togo potrepati.
sentences.l: The women of Rus' wept, saying: now can we neither call to mind our dear husbands in thought, nor think them over in mind, nor behold them with eyes; and of gold and silver — not even a little of it can we handle.
sentences.i: The women of Rus' broke into weeping, crying: 'No longer can we so much as picture our dear husbands in thought, dwell on them in mind, or see them with our own eyes — nor touch so much as a little gold or silver.'
sentences.n: ладъ (gen. pl. of ладо, 'beloved, husband' — the folk-poetic word behind modern лад/ладо) names the women's husbands, presumably fallen or captured. The triple negation мыслію смыслити / думою сдумати / очима съглядати (three near-synonymous verbs for mental and visual apprehension, each with its own instrumental noun) is a deliberate rhetorical build: not even in thought, not even in mind, not even with the eyes. «злата и сребра ... потрепати» ('to handle gold and silver') likely alludes to a dowry or a husband's plunder-gifts, now permanently out of reach; the exact economic sense is not spelled out further. This is the poem's second collective lament of Rus' women, answered and expanded by Yaroslavna's Lament later (part 8).

sentences.t: А въстона бо, братіе, Кіевъ тугою, а Черниговъ напастьми; тоска разліяся по Руской земли; печаль жирна тече средь земли Рускый; а Князи сами на себе крамолу коваху; а поганіи сами побѣдами нарищуще на Рускую землю, емляху дань по бѣлѣ отъ двора.
sentences.tr: A vŭstona bo, bratie, Kievŭ tugoju, a Černigovŭ napastĭmi; toska razlijasja po Ruskoj zemli; pečalĭ žirna teče sredĭ zemli Ruskyj; a Knjazi sami na sebe kramolu kovaxu; a poganii sami pobědami narišcušče na Ruskuju zemlju, emljaxu danĭ po bělě otŭ dvora.
sentences.l: And Kiev groaned, brothers, with anguish, and Chernigov with misfortunes; melancholy has spread across the land of Rus'; rich sorrow flows amid the Russian land; and the princes kept forging treachery among themselves; and the pagans, riding about in victory upon the land of Rus', kept taking tribute, a white [coin] from every household.
sentences.i: And Kiev groaned, brothers, with grief, and Chernigov with misfortunes; sorrow has poured out across the land of Rus'; a rich sadness flows through the Russian land; the princes went on forging treachery against one another, while the pagans rode in triumph across the land of Rus', exacting tribute, a coin from every hearth.
sentences.n: This sentence shifts tenses mid-stream: the aorists въстона, разліяся (single completed events — Kiev groaned once, sorrow spread once) give way to the present тече ('flows,' an ongoing state) and then to the imperfects коваху and емляху (repeated, habitual actions — the princes 'kept' feuding, the pagans 'kept' collecting tribute), with нарищуще as an accompanying present participle describing the pagans' manner as they did so ('riding about in victory'), tracing the disaster from a single blow into a standing condition. печаль жирна ('rich/fat sorrow') echoes жирня времена in unit 4; both are debated but consistently read as intensifiers ('sorrow in abundance'). «по бѣлѣ отъ двора» ('a white [unit] from each household') names a tribute payment, probably a silver coin or, in some readings, the white squirrel-pelt (бѣла вѣверица) used as a unit of tribute in early Rus'; which is meant here is not certain, and we do not choose between them.

sentences.t: Тіи бо два храбрая Святъславлича, Игорь и Всеволодъ уже лжу убуди, которую то бяше успилъ отецъ ихъ Святъславь грозный Великый Кіевскый.
sentences.tr: Tii bo dva xrabraja Svjatŭslavliča, Igorĭ i Vsevolodŭ uže lžu ubudi, kotoruju to bjaše uspilŭ otecĭ ixŭ Svjatŭslavĭ groznyj Velikyj Kievskyj.
sentences.l: For these two brave Svyatoslavichi, Igor and Vsevolod, have now awoken the Lie which their father, Svyatoslav the terrible, great [prince] of Kiev, had put to sleep.
sentences.i: For these two brave Svyatoslavichi, Igor and Vsevolod, have stirred back to life the very discord their father, Svyatoslav the Dread, great prince of Kiev, had long since lulled to sleep.
sentences.n: лжу ('the Lie, falsehood' — acc. of лъжа) stands here for personified discord and injustice among the Rus' princes, continuing the poem's recurring idea (cf. part 3's Oleg 'sowing strife') that internal wrongdoing, not the pagans, is the poem's real antagonist. бяше успилъ is a genuine pluperfect (the auxiliary бяше, imperfect of быти, plus the past participle успилъ, 'had put to sleep') — distinct from the simple aorist and imperfect forms elsewhere, marking an action completed before another past action: the father's earlier pacification, before the sons' present re-awakening of it. Грозный ('the Terrible/Dread') is this historical Svyatoslav III of Kiev's own epithet, centuries before it became attached to Ivan IV.

sentences.t: Грозою бяшеть; притрепеталъ своими сильными плъкы и харалужными мечи; наступи на землю Половецкую; притопта хлъми и яругы; взмути рѣки и озеры; иссуши потоки и болота, а поганаго Кобяка изъ луку моря отъ желѣзныхъ великихъ плъковъ Половецкихъ, яко вихръ выторже: и падеся Кобякъ въ градѣ Кіевѣ, въ гридницѣ Святъславли.
sentences.tr: Grozoju bjašetĭ; pritrepetalŭ svoimi silĭnymi plŭky i xaralužnymi meči; nastupi na zemlju Poloveckuju; pritopta xlŭmi i jarugy; vzmuti rěki i ozery; issuši potoki i bolota, a poganago Kobjaka izŭ luku morja otŭ želěznyxŭ velikixŭ plŭkovŭ Poloveckyxŭ, jako vixrŭ vytorže: i padesja Kobjakŭ vŭ gradě Kievě, vŭ gridnicě Svjatŭslavli.
sentences.l: He was a terror; with his strong regiments and kharalug swords he set [all] trembling; he marched upon the Polovtsian land; he trampled down hills and ravines; he stirred up rivers and lakes; he dried up streams and marshes; and the pagan Kobyak, from the sea's bend, out of the great iron regiments of the Polovtsians, he plucked out like a whirlwind: and Kobyak fell in the city of Kiev, in Svyatoslav's hall.
sentences.i: He was fearsome: with his mighty hosts and hardened kharalug blades he set the very land trembling; he marched into Polovtsian territory, trampled its hills and ravines, churned its rivers and lakes, dried up its streams and marshes — and the pagan Kobyak, out of the great iron ranks of the Polovtsians by the bend of the sea, he plucked out like a whirlwind. And Kobyak fell in the city of Kiev, in Svyatoslav's own hall.
sentences.n: This describes the historical Grand Prince Svyatoslav III Vsevolodovich of Kiev's real 1184 campaign against Khan Kobyak on the Orel River, also recorded in the Hypatian Chronicle — one of the poem's few unambiguous historical anchors amid its darker places. харалужными мечи ('kharalug swords') is the same legendary hard steel met in parts 2 and 3. падеся ('fell,' aorist reflexive) reads as both 'was brought low' and 'fell down,' since Kobyak was in fact captured and brought to Kiev alive, not killed — 'fell . . . in Svyatoslav's hall' pictures his humbling captivity there rather than his death. яко вихръ выторже ('plucked him out like a whirlwind') is a vivid simile for how completely Svyatoslav's strike removed Kobyak from his own army.

sentences.t: Ту Нѣмци и Венедици, ту Греци и Морава поютъ славу Святъславлю, кають Князя Игоря, иже погрузи жиръ во днѣ Каялы рѣкы Половецкія, Рускаго злата насыпаша.
sentences.tr: Tu Němci i Venedici, tu Greci i Morava pojutŭ slavu Svjatŭslavlju, kajutĭ Knjazja Igorja, iže pogruzi žirŭ vo dně Kajaly rěky Poloveckija, Ruskago zlata nasypaša.
sentences.l: There the Germans and Venedici, there the Greeks and Moravians sing the glory of Svyatoslav, [and] reproach Prince Igor, who sank [his] wealth in the bottom of the Kayala, the Polovtsian river; [his men] poured out Russian gold.
sentences.i: There the Germans and the Venedici, there the Greeks and the Moravians sing Svyatoslav's praises — and lay the blame on Prince Igor, who let his wealth sink to the bottom of the Kayala, that Polovtsian river, spilling Russian gold there.
sentences.n: A striking image of the poem's own contemporary fame: the peoples named (Germans; Венедици, either Venetians or the Baltic Wends — itself debated; Greeks; Moravians) are already singing of Svyatoslav's Kobyak victory while blaming Igor for his own defeat, meaning news of the 1185 campaign had already spread across Europe by the time of writing. жиръ is a genuine crux: it can mean 'fat, wealth, abundance' — reinforced here by the same sentence's 'Рускаго злата насыпаша,' Russian gold — or, in an alternative reading some scholars propose, 'the best part, the flower [of an army]'; so погрузи жиръ may mean either 'sank his wealth' or 'drowned the flower of his host' at the Kayala; we keep the literal wording and do not choose between the readings. насыпаша (aorist 3pl, 'they poured/scattered') shifts to a plural subject, presumably Igor's men, describing gold lost with them; Венедици is left untransliterated as a proper name rather than translated, since which people it names is itself uncertain.

sentences.t: Ту Игорь Князь высѣдѣ изъ сѣдла злата, а въ сѣдло Кощіево; уныша бо градомъ забралы, а веселіе пониче.
sentences.tr: Tu Igorĭ Knjazĭ vysědě izŭ sědla zlata, a vŭ sědlo Koščievo; unyša bo gradomŭ zabraly, a veselie poniče.
sentences.l: There Prince Igor got down out of the golden saddle, and into a captive's saddle; for the ramparts have grown despondent throughout the towns, and gladness has drooped.
sentences.i: There Prince Igor stepped down from his golden saddle into the saddle of a captive — the town walls themselves grew despondent, and all gladness has wilted away.
sentences.n: сѣдло Кощіево ('the saddle of a captive/bondsman,' from кощѣй, 'captive, slave') marks Igor's capture in stark physical terms — from a prince's golden saddle to a captive's plain one; кощѣй is the same word that later gives Russian folklore its villain Кощей Безсмертный ('Koshchei the Deathless'), though the two are not to be identified, only related in origin. This unit closes the movement on пониче ('has drooped, wilted'), directly echoing ничить ('droops') that opened it in unit 1 — the poet's own ring-composition, nature's mourning framing the whole passage.

glossary.аркучи: аркучи — saying, exclaiming (present participle; dialectal variant of рекучи, from рещи 'to say')
glossary.бяше: быти — had (been) (imperfect 3sg, auxiliary in the pluperfect 'бяше успилъ')
glossary.бѣлѣ: бѣла — a 'white' [tribute unit], probably a silver coin or a white squirrel-pelt (dat. sg., distributive 'по бѣлѣ' = 'one each'); exact referent debated
glossary.великое: великый — the great (thing) (acc. sg. neut., substantivized)
glossary.венедици: Венедици — the Venedici (nom. pl.): Venetians, or possibly the Baltic Wends; identity debated
glossary.во: въ — in, at (prep. + loc.; form used before a consonant cluster)
glossary.вступилъ: въступити — stepped, entered (past tense, masc. sg.); grammatically mismatched with the feminine subject обида carried over from the previous unit — see note
glossary.въсплакашась: въсплакатися — wept, burst into weeping (aorist 3pl, reflexive)
glossary.въсплескала: въсплескати — clapped, splashed (past tense, fem. sg.)
glossary.въстала: въстати — has arisen (past tense/perfect, fem. sg., not aorist)
glossary.грозный: грозный — terrible, dread (nom. sg.); the historical Svyatoslav III's own epithet
glossary.грозою: гроза — a terror (instr. sg., predicate use with бяшеть: 'he was [as] a terror')
glossary.дажь-божа: Дажьбогъ — Dazhbog's (possessive adj., gen. sg.); the pagan sun-god, an ancestor-figure of the Rus'/princes (spelled Дажь- here; Даждь- in part 3 — an orthographic inconsistency of the 1800 print itself)
glossary.два: дъва — two (num., masc.; governs the dual forms Святъславлича, храбрая)
glossary.двора: дворъ — household, homestead (gen. sg., 'from each household')
glossary.дону: Донъ — the Don (dat. sg.); the river
glossary.думою: дума — with thought, with mind (instr. sg.)
glossary.жалощами: жалощи — sorrows (instr. pl.; cognate with modern жалость)
glossary.жирна: жирный — rich, abundant (nom. sg. fem., short form)
glossary.жирня: жирный — fat, abundant (acc. pl., short form); debated sense — see note
glossary.жиръ: жиръ — wealth, abundance; or, in an alternative reading some scholars propose, 'the best part, the flower [of an army]' (acc. sg.); debated — see note
glossary.жля: Жля — Zhlya (nom. sg.); a personified cry of mourning, from жаль 'pity, sorrow'
glossary.зайде: зайти — has flown off, has gone (aorist 3sg)
glossary.злата: златъ / злато — golden (adj., gen. sg. neut., agreeing with сѣдла); also 'gold' the noun (gen. sg. of злато, in 'Рускаго злата насыпаша', 'poured out Russian gold')
glossary.карна: Карна — Karna (nom. sg.); a personified cry of mourning, from карити 'to lament the dead'
glossary.каялы: Каяла — the river Kayala (gen. sg.; unidentified)
glossary.князя: кънязь — prince (acc. sg., in apposition to Игоря)
glossary.кобяка: Кобякъ — Kobyak (acc./gen. sg.); a historical Polovtsian khan defeated by Svyatoslav III in 1184
glossary.кобякъ: Кобякъ — Kobyak (nom. sg.); the same Polovtsian khan
glossary.которую: который — which (rel. pron., acc. sg. fem., referring back to лжу)
glossary.кощіево: кощѣй — a captive's, a bondsman's (possessive adj., nom./acc. sg.); the same word that later gives Russian folklore its Кощей Безсмертный, though not to be identified with it here
glossary.крѣсити: крѣсити — to revive, to raise up (infinitive); cf. modern воскресение 'resurrection'
glossary.кіевскый: кіевскый — of Kiev, Kievan (nom. sg., adj.)
glossary.лжу: лъжа — the Lie, falsehood (acc. sg.); personified discord/injustice
glossary.луку: лука — bend, curve (gen. sg., 'from the bend of the sea')
glossary.малое: малый — the small (thing) (acc. sg. neut., substantivized)
glossary.млъвити: мълвити — to noisily assert, to wrangle over (infinitive)
glossary.моеже: мой + же — mine also, mine as well (nom. sg. neut. + emphatic particle)
glossary.нарищуще: нарискати — riding about, careering (present active participle)
glossary.обида: обида — offense, wrong (nom. sg.); personified here as an actor
glossary.очима: око — with eyes (instr. dual — the dual number, as elsewhere in the poem for paired body parts)
glossary.пониче: поничи — has drooped, has wilted (aorist 3sg); echoes ничить in unit 1
glossary.преклонилось: преклонитися — has bent down (past tense/perfect, reflexive, neut. sg., not aorist)
glossary.прикрыла: прикрыти — has covered (past tense/perfect, fem. sg., not aorist)
glossary.притрепеталъ: притрепетати — set trembling, struck with terror (past tense, masc. sg.)
glossary.пустыни: пустыни — desolation, wasteland (nom. sg.; an old i-stem noun like кънягыни 'princess,' not a plural of пустыня)
glossary.розѣ: рогъ — horn (loc. sg., 'in a horn'; г > з by the second palatalization)
glossary.рускаго: руськый — Russian, of Rus' (gen. sg., adj., agreeing with злата 'gold')
glossary.руской: руськый — Russian, of Rus' (loc. sg. fem., adj.)
glossary.рускую: руськый — Russian, of Rus' (acc. sg. fem., adj.)
glossary.рускый: руськый — Russian, of Rus' (gen./loc. sg. fem., archaic short ending, agreeing with земли)
glossary.рускія: руськый — Russian, of Rus' (nom. pl. fem., agreeing with жены)
glossary.святъславли: Святъславль — Svyatoslav's (possessive adj., loc. sg. fem., agreeing with гридницѣ)
glossary.святъславлича: Святъславличь — the two Svyatoslavichi, sons of Svyatoslav (nom. dual)
glossary.святъславь: Святъславъ — Svyatoslav (nom. sg.); Svyatoslav III Vsevolodovich, Grand Prince of Kiev
glossary.сдумати: съдумати — to think over, to conceive (infinitive)
glossary.се: се — this (dem. pron., neut. sg.); also 'behold, lo' as a particle (cf. part 2)
glossary.смагу: смага — scorching grief, anguish (acc. sg.); an old word combining 'heat/flame' with figurative grief
glossary.смыслити: съмыслити — to conceive, to call to mind (infinitive)
glossary.средь: среди — amid, in the midst of (prep. + gen.); shortened variant of среди (cf. part 3)
glossary.стугою: стуга — anguish, grief (instr. sg.); an old word closely related to туга, used later in this part
glossary.то: то — that (dem. pron.); also a resumptive particle after a relative pronoun ('которую то', 'which indeed')
glossary.трояню: Троянь — Troyan's (possessive adj.); an obscure mythic/historical name, as in parts 1 and 3
glossary.тугою: туга — with anguish, with grief (instr. sg.)
glossary.тіи: тъ — these, those (dem. pron., nom. pl.)
glossary.успилъ: успити — had put to sleep (past participle, masc. sg.; part of the pluperfect 'бяше успилъ')
glossary.харалужными: харалужный — of kharalug [steel], tempered (instr. pl.); a legendary hard steel
glossary.храбраго: храбрый — brave (gen. sg., agreeing with плъку)
glossary.храбрая: храбрый — brave (nom. dual, agreeing with Святъславлича)
glossary.черниговъ: Чрьниговъ — Chernigov (nom. sg.); a city, the seat of Oleg's line
